audits.title: Audit of acute admissions of COPD: standards of care and management in the hospital setting.
audits.setting: 38 UK hospitals (Royal College of Physicians national audit)

cycle1.result: FEV1 recorded in 53%; arterial blood gases in 79% (range 40-100%); oxygen formally prescribed in 64% (range 9-94%); 35% of acidotic hypercapnic cases had no repeat blood gas and 13% received ventilatory support; smoking cessation advice documented in 30% of current smokers.

audits.other_findings: Of 246 severely hypoxic cases, two-thirds had no confirmation of oxygen recovery above LTOT thresholds; performance lowest in patients not under respiratory specialists.
audits.citation: Roberts CM, Ryland I, Lowe D, Kelly Y, Bucknall CE, Pearson MG, et al.. Audit of acute admissions of COPD: standards of care and management in the hospital setting. Eur Respir J. 2001;17(3):343-349. doi:10.1183/09031936.01.17303430. PMID: 11405509.

audits.title: Emergency department management of exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: audit of compliance with evidence-based guidelines.
audits.standard: Evidence-based guidelines (Level A and B) for COPD exacerbation: bronchodilators, methylxanthines, steroids and NIPPV
audits.setting: Four public and one private emergency departments, Melbourne

cycle1.result: 72.4% received short-acting beta-agonist, 37.8% inhaled anticholinergic, 56.6% systemic steroids; NIPPV in 21 patients, 15 with documented acidosis or hypercapnia.

audits.other_findings: Highest compliance was non-use of methylxanthines; greatest deficit was NIPPV.
audits.citation: Considine J, Botti M, Thomas S. Emergency department management of exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: audit of compliance with evidence-based guidelines. Intern Med J. 2011;41(1a):48-54. doi:10.1111/j.1445-5994.2009.02065.x. PMID: 19811556.

audits.title: [Evaluation of the management of COPD exacerbations: an audit in French emergency services].
audits.standard: French national guidelines for management of COPD exacerbations
audits.setting: 16 emergency departments in the RESUVal network (Rhône valley)

cycle1.result: Respiratory rate and sputum description recorded in 99 (45%) records; oxygen given to 215 (97%), beta-2-agonist aerosols 209 (95%), anticholinergic aerosols 176 (80%); systemic corticosteroid 116 (52%), antibiotics 123 (56%); NIV used in only 59% of eligible acidotic patients.

audits.other_findings: The rest of the initial assessment was generally satisfactory; authors recommend systematic recording of respiratory rate and sputum and more use of NIV.
audits.citation: Hernu R, Eydoux N, Peiretti A, El-Khoury C, Robert D, Argaud L, et al.. [Evaluation of the management of COPD exacerbations: an audit in French emergency services]. Rev Pneumol Clin. 2013;69(3):126-131. doi:10.1016/j.pneumo.2013.01.008. PMID: 23561900.

audits.title: Audit of acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease at Waitemata District Health Board, New Zealand.
audits.standard: Evidence-based guidelines for acute exacerbations of COPD
audits.setting: Waitemata District Health Board hospitals, Auckland

cycle1.result: Good adherence in several areas; room for improvement in NIV use, ABG and spirometry measurement and pulmonary rehabilitation referral (figures not given in abstract).

audits.other_findings: 195 admissions in 156 patients; mean age 73.1; 96% ever-smokers.
audits.citation: Johnson C, Connolly MJ, Clover S, Campbell L, Goonan R, Salmon E, et al.. Audit of acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease at Waitemata District Health Board, New Zealand. N Z Med J. 2013;126(1378):15-25. PMID: 24045312.

audits.title: Treatment of COPD Exacerbation in Switzerland: Results and Recommendations of the European COPD Audit.

cycle1.result: About 43% of Swiss patients with severe AECOPD were current smokers at admission vs 33% in other European countries.

audits.other_findings: Seven recommendations made to improve and standardise management of severe AECOPD in Switzerland.
audits.citation: Buess M, Schilter D, Schneider T, Maurer M, Borer H, Thurnheer R, et al.. Treatment of COPD Exacerbation in Switzerland: Results and Recommendations of the European COPD Audit. Respiration. 2017;94(4):355-365. doi:10.1159/000477911. PMID: 28719893.

audits.title: Management of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbations at the Nasser Medical Complex: a clinical audit.

cycle1.result: All received inhaled bronchodilators; SABA 36 (65%), SAMA 43 (78%); systemic steroids 53 (96%), but 43 (78%) took more than 40 mg prednisolone daily and only 12 (22%) had the 5-day course; oxygen 51 (93%); antibiotics 55 (100%).

audits.other_findings: More patients received SAMA than first-line SABA; documentation was of a very poor standard.
audits.citation: Al-Faqawi M, Abuowda Y, Elmassry AE, Böttcher B. Management of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbations at the Nasser Medical Complex: a clinical audit. Lancet. 2018;391 Suppl 2:S5. doi:10.1016/s0140-6736(18)30371-4. PMID: 29553450.

audits.title: An audit of patients admitted to hospital in Nepal for COPD exacerbation.
audits.standard: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) guidelines
audits.setting: Two Nepalese hospitals including Dhulikhel Hospital

cycle1.result: All received oxygen; 103 (95.4%) short-acting beta2 agonists; 105 (97.2%) antibiotics; 80 (74.5%) systemic corticosteroids; 72 (75.8%) discharged on long-term oxygen.

audits.other_findings: 97 (90.6%) were GOLD group D; unclear whether treatments were given on correct indications, possibly over-treatment.
audits.citation: Styrvold M, Heggset Sterten AJ, Shrestha S, Dhakal S, Harstad I. An audit of patients admitted to hospital in Nepal for COPD exacerbation. SAGE Open Med. 2022;10:20503121221085087. doi:10.1177/20503121221085087. PMID: 35321460.

audits.title: The Management of Acute Exacerbations in COPD: A Retrospective Observational Study and Clinical Audit.
audits.standard: GOLD 2019 report recommendations and previous audits
audits.setting: Emergency department of a public teaching hospital (Cantonal Hospital Baselland)

cycle1.result: 226 visits. GOLD stage documented 81.0%, smoking status 91.6%, GOLD risk category 36%; respiratory rate measured 73%; blood gas 70%; chest imaging 94%; spirometry 10%; short-acting bronchodilators 56%; systemic steroids 86%; antibiotics 56%; NIV in 25% of indicated cases; smoking cessation advice 26% of smokers; pulmonary rehabilitation referral 16%.

audits.other_findings: In one fourth of antibiotic prescriptions the indication was not clear.
audits.citation: Boesing M, Ottensarendt N, Lüthi-Corridori G, Leuppi JD. The Management of Acute Exacerbations in COPD: A Retrospective Observational Study and Clinical Audit. J Clin Med. 2023;13(1):19. doi:10.3390/jcm13010019. PMID: 38202025.

audits.title: Pain and Dyspnea During Acute Exacerbations of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: Documentation Audit 2019-2020.
audits.setting: Metropolitan hospital, Melbourne; inpatients with acute exacerbation of COPD

cycle1.result: Pain assessed with a PROM in 99% and dyspnoea in 8% of cases.

audits.other_findings: All PROMs measured symptom intensity; focal periods rarely reported for pain.
audits.citation: Clarke SY, Williams MT, Johnston KN, Lee AL. Pain and Dyspnea During Acute Exacerbations of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: Documentation Audit 2019-2020. J Clin Med. 2025;14(1):252. doi:10.3390/jcm14010252. PMID: 39797334.
